---
title: "Plotting Causal Graphs"
knitr:
  opts_chunk:
    collapse: true
    comment: "#>"
---

```{r}
#| label: setup

library(CausalStructures)
setup()
```

`plot()` draws a `cgraph` with grid graphics. Every aspect of the drawing can be
modified, which we will show below.

## A first plot

All edges are rendered according to their actual edge marks:

```{r}
#| label: first-plot

unknown <- cgraph(A %-->% B %---% C %o->% D %o-o% A, class = "UNKNOWN")
plot(unknown)
```

Now we will showcase how to make adjustments to the plotting

## Layouts

`layout` accepts a method name, a layout function, or a pre-computed
`data.frame` of `name`/`x`/`y` coordinates. The named methods (`"stress"`,
`"spring"`, `"sfdp"`, `"spectral"`, `"shell"`, `"squaregrid"`, `"circle"`) all
come from [NetworkLayout.jl](https://github.com/JuliaGraphs/NetworkLayout.jl);
see `?cgraph_layout` for what each does.

```{r}
#| label: layout-spring

dag <- cgraph(A %-->% X + Y, X %-->% M, M %-->% Y)
plot(dag, layout = "spring", main = "Spring layout")
```

Alternatively you can pass a pre-computed layout, useful for when comparing
different graphs with the same nodes:

```{r}
#| label: layout-fixed

fixed <- data.frame(
  name = c("A", "X", "Y", "M"),
  x = c(0, 1, 2, 1.5),
  y = c(1, 1, 1, 0)
)
plot(dag, layout = fixed, main = "Fixed coordinates")
```

Notice the automatic curve on the edge from $A$ to $Y$ to avoid it passing
through $X$!

## Styling nodes

`node_style` accepts anything `grid::gpar()` understands (`fill`, `col`, `lwd`,
`lty`, `alpha`) plus two geometry options: `padding` (text padding inside the
node, in mm; default 2) and `size` (a multiplier on the computed node radius;
default 1). `by_node` overrides any of these per node.

```{r}
#| label: node-style

plot(
  dag,
  node_style = list(
    fill = "lightblue",
    col = "navy",
    lwd = 2,
    size = 1.3,
    by_node = list(
      Y = list(fill = "gold"),
      M = list(fill = "white", col = "gray60", size = 0.8)
    )
  ),
  main = "Node styling"
)
```

## Styling edges

`edge_style` also accepts `grid::gpar()` fields (`col`, `lwd`, `lty`, `alpha`,
`fill`) plus `arrow_size` (mm, default 3), `circle_size` (mm, default 1.5, for
the `o->`/`o--`/`o-o` endpoint marks), and `route` (logical, default `TRUE`:
bend an edge around a non-incident node it would otherwise cross).

Arrowhead `fill` defaults to the edge's own `col`, so arrowheads render solid by
default and recolor along with the edge. Pass `fill = NA` for the classic
hollow/outline arrowhead:

```{r}
#| label: edge-fill

plot(
  dag,
  edge_style = list(col = "darkgreen", fill = NA, lwd = 1.5)
)
```

### Per-edge overrides (`by_edge`)

`by_edge` is a named list keyed by node name. A node-wide entry (a plain style
list) applies to every edge touching that node; a nested entry
(`A = list(B = list(...))`) targets one specific edge and wins over any
node-wide setting for the same edge.

```{r}
#| label: edge-by-edge

plot(
  dag,
  edge_style = list(
    col = "gray50",
    by_edge = list(
      # Node-wide: every edge touching X...
      X = list(col = "steelblue"),
      # ...except X -> M specifically
      M = list(X = list(col = "red", lwd = 3))
    )
  ),
  main = "by_edge overrides"
)
```

### Per-edge-type styling

`edge_style` can also carry `directed`, `undirected`, `bidirected`, and
`partial` sub-lists (the last covers any edge with a `o->`/`o-o`/`--o` endpoint
mark). Style precedence, highest to lowest: specific edge in `by_edge` >
node-wide entry in `by_edge` > edge-type style > global style.

```{r}
#| label: edge-per-type

mixed <- cgraph("A --> B, B --- C, C <-> D, D o-> E", class = "UNKNOWN")
plot(
  mixed,
  layout = "circle",
  edge_style = list(
    directed = list(col = "black"),
    undirected = list(col = "forestgreen", lwd = 2),
    bidirected = list(col = "purple"),
    partial = list(col = "orange", circle_size = 2)
  ),
  main = "Styling by edge type"
)
```

## Styling labels

`label_style` sets the node-label text appearance: `col`, `fontsize`,
`fontface`, `fontfamily`, `cex`.

```{r}
#| label: label-style

plot(
  dag,
  label_style = list(col = "white", fontface = "bold", fontsize = 12),
  node_style = list(fill = "steelblue4"),
  main = "Label styling"
)
```

## Titles

`main` sets the plot title; `title_style` accepts the same fields as
`label_style`.

```{r}
#| label: title-style

plot(
  dag,
  main = "Custom title",
  title_style = list(col = "darkred", fontsize = 18, fontface = "italic")
)
```

## Aspect ratio and margins

`asp` fixes the y/x aspect ratio of the plotted data (`NA`, the default, fills
the available space; `asp = 1` makes one x-unit equal one y-unit).
`outer_margin` and `title_gap` are `grid::unit()`s controlling the margin around
the whole plot and the gap between the title and the graph.

```{r}
#| label: asp

plot(dag, asp = 1, main = "asp = 1")
```

## Putting it together

```{r}
#| label: combined

plot(
  dag,
  node_style = list(
    fill = "white",
    col = "black",
    by_node = list(Y = list(fill = "gold", col = "darkorange", lwd = 2))
  ),
  edge_style = list(
    col = "gray40",
    by_edge = list(X = list(M = list(col = "red", lwd = 2)))
  ),
  label_style = list(fontface = "bold"),
  main = "Everything at once",
  title_style = list(fontsize = 16)
)
```
